rows.name: Qur'an
rows.detail: Explicit: 2:283 provides for a pledge (rahn) held as security when no scribe can record a debt on a journey.
rows.detail_long: 'If you are on a journey and cannot find a scribe, then a pledge in hand' — the one contract of the ten with a verse that names it. Tafsir on this verse (Tabari, Qurtubi — both in the app) reads the pledge as security for debt.
rows.internal_ref: Verse + tafsir passages on 2:283 extracted verbatim from app files this session (kafalah_source_extract.json)

rows.name: Sahih Bukhari 2068
rows.detail: The Prophet bought food grains from a Jewish merchant on credit and mortgaged his iron armor — the living rahn precedent.
rows.detail_long: Aisha's narration: the Prophet's own armor pledged for barley. The same narration anchors credit purchase (and qard); Bukhari's pledge chapters build on it. App grading Sahih.

rows.name: Jami' al-Tirmidhi 1214
rows.detail: Ibn Abbas: the Prophet died while his armour was pawned for twenty sa' of food for his family.
rows.detail_long: App text read verbatim, from Tirmidhi's Business chapters with his own grading preserved ('This Hadith is Hasan Sahih'): the pledge outstanding at the Prophet's death — rahn practised to the very end, for household provisions. The strongest possible endorsement-by-practice of secured debt.

rows.name: Bulugh al-Maram 985
rows.detail: Usufruct of the pledge for its upkeep. The pledged animal may be ridden, its milk drunk — by whoever bears its upkeep. Benefit follows expense, even inside a pledge.
rows.detail_long: App text read verbatim: 'An animal may be ridden, due to what is spent on it, when it is in pledge; and the milk of a camel may be drunk, due to what is spent on it... the responsibility of spending on it is upon the one who rides and drinks.' The pledge is not sterile: whoever maintains the collateral takes its usufruct — the maintenance-benefit symmetry classical rahn law builds on.

rows.internal_ref: Record read verbatim from app hadith file (batch4_source_extract.json, 2026-07-14)

rows.name: Ibn Abbas (attrib., Tanwir al-Miqbas)
rows.detail: The earliest attributed gloss on 2:283: on a journey with no scribe, 'let the creditor take from the indebted person a security for his loan' — and trust without security binds the debtor's conscience.
rows.detail_long: Tanwir al-Miqbas (in the app) on 2:283: the pledge-in-hand substitutes for the written record when writing is unavailable; and where a loan is extended on pure trust, the trusted party must 'deliver up that which is entrusted to him' and fear Allah in repayment. Security and conscience presented as the verse's two enforcement tracks. Attribution traditional, not critical — hence 'attrib.'
rows.evidence_display: Tanwir al-Miqbas (attrib. Ibn Abbas), on Q2:283 (text in app)
rows.internal_ref: Passage read verbatim from app tafsir file (batch4_source_extract.json, 2026-07-14)

rows.name: Ibn Kathir
rows.detail: Ibn Kathir on 2:283: the pledge stands in for the missing scribe — citing Ibn Abbas: even a scribe without paper, ink or pen triggers it.
rows.detail_long: The app's Ibn Kathir passage on 2:283 (read this session): travel plus deferred debt plus no scribe = 'let there be a pledge taken (mortgaging) given to the creditor'; and Ibn Abbas widens the trigger — 'even if they find a scribe, but did not find paper, ink or pen'. The pledge as the documentation-substitute, its scope read generously.
rows.evidence_display: Tafsir Ibn Kathir, on Q2:283 (text in app)
rows.internal_ref: Passage read verbatim from app tafsir file (batch4_source_extract.json, 2026-07-14)

rows.detail: Al-Mughni's Kitab al-Rahn sets the Hanbali pledge rules; all four schools accept rahn.
rows.detail_long: Possession, custody, whose risk, and whether the creditor may use the pledged asset — the standard classical questions, answered per school. App book F0749-B50. rows.name: AAOIFI
rows.work_title: Shari'ah Standard No. 39 (Mortgage and Its Contemporary Applications)
rows.detail: AAOIFI Shari'ah Standard No. 39 (2009) codifies rahn for modern use: mortgaging shares, sukuk, investment accounts, income streams and insured assets.
rows.detail_long: SS39 modernizes the pledge: what may be mortgaged (including fungibles, units, accounts), mortgage of income yet to be owned, insurance of the pledged asset, and the creditor's rights — the standard behind today's Islamic collateral packages and ar-rahnu schemes. VERIFIED: adopted 12-15 March 2009 (meeting 23, Bahrain). This also closes the earlier gap where Rahn had no confirmed dedicated standard. VERIFIED THIS SESSION (SS39 full text, ss3.txt): adoption 12-15 March 2009, Bahrain (meeting 23). CLAUSES VERIFIED-TO-TEXT: 3/1/1 the mortgage binds the mortgagor once concluded; only the mortgagee may revoke; 3/2/1 the mortgaged asset must be Shari'ah-permissible, well specified and deliverable; 3/3/1 the secured debt must itself be permissible (sale income, guarantee, salam or istisna'a commodity, owed usufruct); 3/4/1 on default the mortgagee may claim sale of the asset — any surplus after the debt returns to the mortgagor; 4/3 interest-based bonds, preference shares and the like may not be mortgaged.
rows.internal_ref: Verified from the official AAOIFI Shari'ah Standards 2015 full text (user-supplied PDF, adoption page read this session) | SS39 adoption + clauses read verbatim from ss3.txt (2026-07-14)
